general.about: Any agent whose client name has no record of its own: no own way to receive an event is assumed, so a host, a blind channel under its conditions, or the journal delivers.
general.source: Skein monitor contract: the method order and the addressee rule of the general record (agent process = nearest ancestor of the runner that is neither the loader, the runner nor a listed shell).
warnings: The client name was not found in the registry; the general record is used.

agents.about: Claude Code: the runner's stdout lines become turns through its Monitor tool; Zavod engines claude, kimi and zai-claude run this harness.
agents.source: code.claude.com/docs tools-reference, 'Monitor tool' (timeout_ms: 5 minutes by default, at most 30 minutes; deadlines above 1800000 ms are capped; available on Windows only with Git Bash); Claude Code 2.1.331 (native executable 'claude', 'claude.exe' on Windows).

methods.instruction: Run `command` with the Monitor tool, timeout_ms 1800000 (its maximum, 30 minutes). Each stdout line is an event of the monitor. When Monitor reports the command ended at its deadline, start it with Monitor again: the cursor is kept, no event is lost.

agents.about: Grok Build: the runner's stdout lines become turns through its monitor tool.
agents.source: github.com/xai-org/grok-build 2bdd1d6 (1.0.45; npm @xai-official/grok 1.0.92): crates/codegen/xai-grok-tools/src/implementations/grok_build/monitor/tool.rs#MonitorTool (every stdout line is one MonitorEvent), monitor/types.rs#DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS (10 h unless persistent), #RATE_LIMIT_CAPACITY (10 events, one more every 2 s, extra lines suppressed), #AUTO_KILL_THRESHOLD_MS (the monitor is killed after 30 s of suppression); executable 'grok' (bin/grok-native).

methods.instruction: Run `command` with the monitor tool, persistent: true. Each stdout line is an event of the monitor.

agents.about: Kimi Code in its terminal UI: the runner exits after a batch of events, and the end of the background command wakes the agent; Zavod engine nkimi runs this harness.
agents.source: github.com/MoonshotAI/kimi-code 48cdb62 (2.7.3): loop-actor.ts#drainDetachedCompletions (a finished background Bash command starts a turn; the output of a running one does not), Bash tool parameters run_in_background and disable_timeout (without it a background command ends timed_out); Git Bash on Windows (KIMI_SHELL_PATH); npm @moonshot-ai/kimi-code 2.8.0 dist/main.mjs#PROCESS_NAME (process title 'kimi-code', command 'kimi').

methods.instruction: Run `command` with the Bash tool, run_in_background=true, disable_timeout=true, and a description of your choice. It ends after a batch of events with a stop line; handle the events, then follow the action of that line.

agents.about: Codex CLI in a terminal: the runner detaches and queues each event into the agent's own thread with codex queue.
agents.source: github.com/openai/codex ae21235afbd5ba6556c2ab4b64f6afc96a139ef8 (codex-rs): core/src/exec_env.rs (every command of a thread gets CODEX_THREAD_ID and CODEX_SESSION_ID); cli/src/queue_cmd.rs#QueueCommand (--thread, --message; --remote selects a remote app server, whose address no variable of the agent's commands carries, so a thread on a remote server has no source of its address); native executable 'codex' started by the npm wrapper bin/codex.js.

methods.instruction: Run `command` once in a shell: it returns after the line {"event":"monitor_started",...} and the monitor queues every event into this thread with codex queue on its own; a queued message starts a turn when the thread is idle.

channels.about: codex queue: the own delivery command of Codex, which puts a user message into the queue of a thread by its id; the thread takes it when idle.
channels.source: github.com/openai/codex ae21235afbd5ba6556c2ab4b64f6afc96a139ef8 (codex-rs): cli/src/queue_cmd.rs#QueueCommand and tui/src/session_queue_commands.rs#run_session_queue_command (prints 'Queued message <id> for thread <id>.' and exits 0; the only warning, on stderr, belongs to --resume, which is not passed; an error exits non-zero after the request may have been sent); tui/src/lib.rs#maybe_probe_default_daemon_socket and #app_server_target_for_launch (the local app-server daemon socket is used when it answers, otherwise an embedded app server writes the queue, so the socket is no boundary of the delivery); uds/src/daemon_directory.rs#shared_daemon_socket_directory (the socket lives under /tmp/codex-daemon-<uid>, hidden by sandboxes); state/src/lib.rs#SQLITE_HOME_ENV and utils/home-dir find_codex_home (the queue is in the SQLite state database under CODEX_SQLITE_HOME, else CODEX_HOME, else ~/.codex); protocol/src/user_input.rs#MAX_USER_INPUT_TEXT_CHARS (1048576 characters); cli/src/queue_cmd.rs has no platform branch, so Windows runs the same command, by the native codex.exe of the agent process, else codex.exe or the codex.cmd shim of npm that PATH finds (a .cmd takes the id-only text, US-11). The limit of the text is the smallest of the platforms: Windows CreateProcess takes a command line of at most 32767 UTF-16 code units, and the quoting of an argument for it (subprocess.list2cmdline) can double every quote and the backslashes before one, so the text keeps under half of it; Linux execve(2) takes 131072 bytes per argument (MAX_ARG_STRLEN) and macOS a larger ARG_MAX for all arguments together.

probes.source: github.com/openai/codex ae21235afbd5ba6556c2ab4b64f6afc96a139ef8 (codex-rs): state/src/lib.rs#SQLITE_HOME_ENV, utils/home-dir find_codex_home (the directory of the state database that holds the queue).

addressee.limitation: A thread id is a UUID and a new thread gets a new one, so the id is not reused; a closed or interrupted thread still takes the message into its queue (queued, no turn).

channels.about: Zavod: the host delivers the event as a letter to the agent's own address.
channels.source: Zavod CLI: ZAVOD_ME is the agent's address (a UUID equal to ZAVOD_AGENT_ID), ZAVOD_AGENT_ENGINE_ID its engine, ZAVOD_AGENT_ROOT_PID, ZAVOD_AGENT_ROOT_START and ZAVOD_AGENT_ROOT_BOOT_ID the life of its root process (the pid, field 22 of /proc/<pid>/stat and the boot id of the system); the CLI is zavod in PATH or ~/.local/bin/zavod; `zavod --json send <address> --text-file -` takes the body on stdin (a text argument is refused) and prints one JSON envelope with the top-level fields exit_code and code (checked with a refused call: exit_code 11, code letter_too_large, 'nothing was accepted'); exit 0 accepted, 10 partial effect, 11 refused (code caller_not_in_roster: the caller's address is no live agent; code letter_too_large: the body is over 65536 bytes), 12 no connection (nothing sent), 13 unknown outcome, 14 protocol error; a letter holds at most 10000 characters; `zavod --json version` sends nothing; Linux and other POSIX systems only.

probes.source: Zavod CLI: `zavod --json version` prints the versions of the CLI and of Zavod and sends nothing; exit 0 when Zavod answers.

addressee.limitation: After the letter is accepted (exit 0) its delivery is Zavod's: an agent recreated under the same address in that interval gets the letter.

warnings: Events come as Zavod letters from your own address. Do not reply to this letter. Do not clear the input field.
textNotes: Do not reply to this letter.
Do not clear the input field.

channels.about: Orca: a terminal environment whose CLI types the event into the agent's own terminal as a prompt and reports whether the turn started.
channels.source: github.com/stablyai/orca cbeddb92bcc2070da1466c20d31c3223d5e9ac48 (1.4.214): src/main/ipc/pty/ipc/spawn-options.ts (ORCA_TERMINAL_HANDLE in the environment of every PTY, inherited by the agent's commands); src/cli/terminals/terminal-selector.ts#getTerminalHandle (without --terminal a send goes to the active terminal of the worktree, so the handle is passed); src/cli/specs/terminal-send.ts#TERMINAL_SEND_COMMAND_SPEC and src/cli/terminals/terminal-send.ts#terminalSendHandler (--text with --enter is an agent prompt; --wait-submit needs the prompt-delivery capability, else incompatible_runtime; an unreachable host is runtime_unavailable before the send call, 'no input was sent'; accepted:false exits 1; a missing prompt receipt after acceptance is incompatible_runtime too); src/main/runtime/rpc/methods/terminal/terminal-send-method.ts#refusedSend and src/shared/terminal/pty/lifecycle/pty-write-settlement.ts#WriteSettlement (accepted:false without a write settlement is a guard refusal before the write, outcome 'refused' a write declined before any byte reached the transport, 'unverifiable' ambiguous); src/cli/runtime/client.ts#call and src/cli/runtime/connection/terminal-prompt-mutation-recovery.ts (every failure of the send call itself carries error.data.orchestrationRequestId, or deliveryOutcome 'unknown'; runtime_unavailable is also 'Orca closed the connection before responding' after the request: src/cli/runtime/connection/transport.ts); src/main/runtime/terminal/input/terminal-agent-prompt.ts#writeTerminalAgentPrompt (agent_prompt_blocked is checked before the paste and again after it, before Enter: one code on both sides of the transfer); src/main/runtime/terminal/input/orca-runtime-agent-prompt-request-correlation.ts#observeTerminalAgentPrompt (observation incarnation_replaced: the terminal process changed); src/main/runtime/terminal/input/agent-prompt-submission-verification.ts#isTerminalSendSettlementAgent (turn_started only for claude, codex and antigravity); src/cli/specs/core.ts and src/cli/terminals/terminal.ts ('terminal wait --for tui-idle --timeout-ms' exits 1 when the condition is not met; 'terminal show --json' gives result.terminal, src/shared/terminal/runtime/runtime-terminal-contracts.ts#RuntimeTerminalSummary: incarnationId, agentIdentity absent when unknown, connected); src/shared/cli/orca-cli-command-name.ts#getOrcaCliCommandNameForPlatform (orca-ide on Linux, where orca is the GNOME screen reader; orca on macOS; ORCA_CLI_COMMAND in a managed WSL) and src/main/cli/cli-installer.ts (packaged Windows puts resources/bin/orca.exe, the native launcher, on PATH; the orca.cmd shim would take only an id-only text, US-11); src/shared/terminal/input/terminal-input.ts#TERMINAL_INPUT_MAX_BYTES (16 MiB). The text goes in an argument, so its limit is the smallest command line of the platforms: Windows CreateProcess takes at most 32767 UTF-16 code units, and quoting an argument can double its quotes and backslashes, so the text keeps under half of it; Linux execve(2) takes 131072 bytes per argument. --retry-request is not used: a repeat follows only a refusal before send, which sent nothing.

probes.source: github.com/stablyai/orca cbeddb92: src/cli/terminals/terminal.ts ('terminal show' reads the terminal and sends nothing).

addressee.limitation: A terminal whose host gives no incarnationId (an older Orca) is checked by its agent process only.

channels.about: Paseo (agent): the daemon that launched the agent queues each event as a message to the agent's own session.
channels.source: github.com/getpaseo/paseo c1b43ee571ee15f409b4f1374b279f2f94387448 (0.17.4): packages/server/src/server/agent/agent-manager.ts (every agent process the daemon launches gets PASEO_AGENT_ID, its agent UUID, and PASEO_AGENT_CWD); packages/server/src/server/daemon-worker.ts (the daemon process is titled 'Paseo Daemon'; it launches the provider processes: Claude through the Agent SDK, Codex app-server, ACP agents, OpenCode, Pi); packages/cli/src/commands/agent/send.ts#runSendCommand and #buildNoWaitResult (--prompt-file reads the text from a UTF-8 file; from a process with PASEO_AGENT_ID the default behaviour is queue; --no-wait prints {agentId, status, activeTurnBehavior, message}, status 'queued' when the daemon queued it); packages/server/src/server/agent/agent-messages/delivery.ts#QUIET_MS (the queue waits a 2 s quiet window and the end of the running turn, so no idle wait of the runner); packages/cli/src/utils/client.ts#connectToDaemon (DAEMON_UNREACHABLE and AUTH_REQUIRED come from connecting, before the message is sent); packages/cli/src/output/with-output.ts and render.ts#renderError (a result on stdout; an error as {"error":{code,message}} on stderr, exit 1); packages/cli/src/commands/agent/inspect.ts#runInspectCommand (the agent object on stdout: Id, Provider, Status, Archived, CreatedAt; AGENT_NOT_FOUND on stderr; it sends nothing); packages/server/src/server/agent/idle-runtime-cleanup/index.ts#IDLE_PERIOD_MS (an agent idle for an hour is unloaded with its process tree unless agents.idleRuntimeCleanup is false); packages/desktop/src/integrations/cli-install/install.ts#buildCmdTrampoline (the app installs the CLI as ~/.local/bin/paseo, on Windows %USERPROFILE%\.local\bin\paseo.cmd, which the agent's PATH may lack; a .cmd takes the text only by file, US-11). No deduplication: every send is a new message.

probes.source: github.com/getpaseo/paseo c1b43ee5: packages/cli/src/commands/agent/inspect.ts#runInspectCommand (reads the agent from the daemon, sends nothing).

addressee.limitation: An agent id is a UUID the daemon gives; the source does not say whether a session recreated under the same id is told apart.

warnings: Paseo unloads an agent idle for an hour together with its processes, the monitor among them (setting agents.idleRuntimeCleanup); after such an unload start the monitor again.

shells.source: POSIX: shells(5), the /etc/shells list of valid login shells (sh, bash, dash, zsh, ksh, mksh, fish, tcsh, csh, nu, pwsh are the names such lists carry); Windows: Microsoft Learn 'cmd' (cmd.exe), 'about_PowerShell_exe' (powershell.exe) and 'about_Pwsh' (pwsh.exe).
